principle: Structural depletion operates against false signals of escalation through simultaneous resource removal and tempo acceleration, creating contradiction between what diminishes and what amplifies.

nodes.label: Numerical countdown structure
nodes.description: Systematic reduction from seven samurai to three survivors, with each death functioning as structural phase marker dividing the battle sequence into discrete units rather than continuous action.
evidence: Explicitly tracked across all analytical documents and identified as load-bearing constraint.
Each death divides the 77-minute battle into distinct phases rather than undifferentiated combat.
Reinforcement mechanisms and the depletion-escalation paradox both depend on it.

nodes.label: Durational extension of preparation
nodes.description: 60-minute training block with minimal plot advancement, establishing labor investment through repeated similar actions (fence-building, spear practice) with slight variations.
evidence: Dedicated temporal analysis identifies duration itself as structural, not narrative.
Explicitly linked to making subsequent losses register structurally rather than as spectacle.
Validation identifies it as prerequisite for the countdown mechanism.

nodes.label: Circular perimeter as tactical map
nodes.description: Stable village geography established through hand-drawn map shown to characters, maintained with spatial consistency throughout battle sequences to allow viewer tracking of tactical positions at specific compass points.
evidence: Defenders positioned at specific compass points; attacks come from predictable directions based on established geometry.
Identified as structural prerequisite for subsequent formal operations, not exposition.
Contradiction analysis shows the spatial system fails when this constraint is removed in the final phase.
Validation rates it medium-high confidence.
rules: stable circular geometry enables tactical legibility

nodes.label: Tempo acceleration across battle phases
nodes.description: Systematic score tempo progression from 80 BPM in first attack to 140 BPM in final attack, creating linear acceleration independent of visual content through percussive rhythmic cells.
evidence: Attack 1 averages 80 BPM, attack 2 100 BPM, attack 3 120 BPM, attack 4 140 BPM in linear progression.
Validation classifies it as supporting: it reinforces the countdown by creating false escalation against depletion but does not generate the core contradiction alone.

nodes.label: Silence-after-death caesuras
nodes.description: Extended silences of 8 to 15 seconds immediately after each samurai death, plus 90 seconds before the final battle and 25 seconds after victory, functioning as structural punctuation between phases.
evidence: Silence appears at three specific junctures: after each death, night before final battle, and final shot.
Validation notes it converts countdown arithmetic into phase markers but countdown operates without it.

nodes.label: Hand-drawn village map
nodes.description: Map shown to characters that establishes the circular village geography with bisecting stream, functioning as structural prerequisite rather than exposition.
evidence: Geography is established through the drawn map, then maintained with spatial consistency throughout battle sequences.
Stage 2 states the map is not exposition but structural prerequisite for subsequent formal operations.

nodes.label: Depth-staging composition
nodes.description: Action arranged across three or more spatial planes within single frames, compressing multiple narrative threads into unified shots rather than requiring montage.
evidence: Foreground, middle-ground, and background action layered consistently through recruitment and battle scenes.
Validation classifies it as supporting: it amplifies spatial efficiency but could be replaced with montage without destroying the work's identity.

nodes.label: Vertical stratification in combat staging
nodes.description: Elevation differences in battle: samurai on rooftops, bandits on lower ground, villagers in doorways at intermediate height, creating three vertical zones of action in single frames.
evidence: Three vertical zones allow simultaneous tracking of multiple combat threads without cutting.
Stage 2 states vertical staging becomes arbitrary without the geometric constraint.

nodes.label: Negative space as tactical void
nodes.description: Empty zones such as cleared fields around the village perimeter and vacant streets during attacks, functioning as kill zones where any movement is visually salient.
evidence: Voids create kill zones where bandits are exposed; emptiness is functional, not compositional accident.
Stage 2 states negative space loses tactical meaning without the known geometry.

nodes.label: Real-time battle choreography in continuous takes
nodes.description: Individual combat exchanges unfold in continuous takes of 30 to 90 seconds with no accelerated editing, creating temporal parity between viewer and character experience.
evidence: Duration of sword exchanges, running, and falling matches performed duration.
Stage 2 states extended takes become spatially illegible without the geometric constraint.

nodes.label: Recursive attacks with decreasing intervals
nodes.description: Four bandit attacks with progressively shorter intervals between them: roughly 20 minutes, then 15, then 8, accelerating narrative momentum within a fixed four-wave structure.
evidence: Intervals measured explicitly: attack 1 to 2 about 20 minutes, 2 to 3 about 15, 3 to 4 about 8.
Stage 2 identifies interval compression as one register of nested compression carrying acceleration information.

nodes.label: Diegetic-to-nondiegetic score coverage shift
nodes.description: Nondiegetic score covers about 17 percent of the dispersed recruitment section and 68 percent of the concentrated battle section, a fourfold density increase as geography contracts, while ambient sound strips to near-silence.
evidence: Recruitment: roughly 12 minutes of score in 70 minutes; battle: roughly 52 minutes of score in 77 minutes.
Stage 2 establishes a predictive rule allowing tactical position to be read through sonic information alone.

nodes.label: Percussive score architecture
nodes.description: Taiko drums, wood blocks, and struck instruments as primary battle timbres, operating through looping 4 to 8 beat rhythmic cells with no sustained melodic lines.
evidence: Percussive vocabulary matches physical impact sounds of combat such as sword strikes and falling bodies.
The tempo progression is carried by these rhythmic cells.

nodes.label: Final-phase perimeter breach
nodes.description: In the final battle phase, bandits breach the circular perimeter and combat moves to interior spaces where the circular logic cannot operate, producing deliberate spatial confusion.
evidence: Stage 3 states the film continues the same formal techniques without the geometric foundation that made them coherent.
Viewers cannot track position because the enabling constraint has been removed by design.
rule_violations: stable circular geometry enables tactical legibility

nodes.label: Sonic void at Kikuchiyo death
nodes.description: At Kikuchiyo's death, maximum spatial concentration produces near-silence rather than the predicted score density, inverting the spatial-sonic correspondence at the structural climax.
evidence: Stage 3 states the mechanism that predicted sonic density through 140 minutes fails at the moment of greatest load.
This is described as the system contradicting its own operational logic, not suspension for emphasis.

edges.rationale: Durational investment in preparation makes subsequent subtractions register as structural loss: without 60-minute labor accumulation, deaths become narrative events rather than load-bearing subtractions. Validation names M2 a prerequisite for the countdown.

Each samurai death triggers an 8 to 15 second silence caesura that converts casualties into phase markers, preventing the countdown from becoming undifferentiated arithmetic; the countdown survives without it but weakens.
Each caesura resets the tempo baseline higher, so deaths accelerate what remains rather than slowing the work down, strengthening the linear tempo progression.

Tempo acceleration from 80 to 140 BPM creates false expectation of escalation while the samurai count decreases; the sonic register moves opposite to the numerical register, generating the depletion-escalation tension.

As resources deplete from seven to three, tactical effectiveness increases rather than degrades, inverting the expectation that the durational investment established, namely that loss equals degradation.
Attack intervals compress as personnel depletes: 20 minutes between attacks 1 and 2, 15 between 2 and 3, 8 between 3 and 4, accelerating momentum while the samurai count decreases.
Depth-staging composition depends on circular perimeter stability: arranging action across three spatial planes requires known geometry to remain spatially coherent across cuts.
Geometric constraint enables tactical legibility: vertical stratification requires the stable circular perimeter so rooftops, ground, and doorways maintain the same spatial relationships across cuts.
Geometric constraint enables tactical legibility: negative space functions predictably as kill zones only because cleared perimeter zones remain empty under known geometry.

Real-time battle choreography remains spatially coherent across 30 to 90 second continuous takes only because the geography is fixed; without the constraint, extended takes become spatially illegible.

The hand-drawn map shown to characters supplies the warrant for the stable geography; Stage 2 states the map is not exposition but the structural prerequisite establishing the geometry viewers then track.
The linear tempo progression is carried by looping 4 to 8 beat percussive rhythmic cells; without the percussive score architecture there is no vehicle for the systematic BPM acceleration.

Spatial contraction requires sonic replacement: as geography concentrates from dispersed recruitment to circular perimeter, nondiegetic score coverage increases from 17 to 68 percent, letting viewers read tactical position through sound alone.
The final-phase breach removes the enabling geometric condition while the same formal techniques continue, demonstrating the spatial system's dependency by violating it deliberately.
At Kikuchiyo's death maximum spatial concentration produces sonic void rather than predicted score density, inverting the spatial-sonic correspondence rule after 140 minutes of reliable operation.

violated: stable circular geometry enables tactical legibility

failure_modes.consequence: When the circular perimeter constraint fails (as in the final-phase breach), spatial legibility collapses: vertical stratification becomes arbitrary, negative space loses tactical meaning, depth staging loses coherence, and extended takes become spatially illegible.

At Kikuchiyo's death the spatial-sonic correspondence inverts: maximum spatial concentration produces sonic void rather than predicted score density, contradicting 140 minutes of operational logic at the moment of greatest structural load.

If the escalation register is removed, the viewer tracks only attrition; the structural irony of simultaneous escalation and depletion disappears and the work reduces to simple tragedy rather than a contradiction held without reconciliation.

Without the numerical countdown, the battle's phase structure becomes invisible, the fight collapses into undifferentiated action, and victory becomes formally indistinguishable from defeat except by the arithmetic fact of survival.

Without the 60-minute labor accumulation, deaths become narrative events rather than structural losses; the countdown reduces to arithmetic and the depletion-escalation paradox cannot operate because no expectation of loss as degradation has been established.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, the battle becomes undifferentiated action without phase structure; the entire dramatic architecture collapses into generic combat lacking progressive depletion logic.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If removed, deaths lack structural weight because no labor investment is established; the countdown becomes arithmetic rather than tragedy; losses register as narrative events rather than structural
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, spatial coherence collapses; vertical stratification and extended takes become illegible; the viewer cannot track tactical positions and the geometric foundation for formal operations
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the false escalation signal disappears; the contradiction between intensifying tempo and depleting resources collapses into simple attrition narrative without structural irony.
